name: Connecticut

statute.name: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
statute.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-200 et seq. (access § 1-210; appeals § 1-206; fees § 1-212)

response.rule_text: Any denial must be made in writing within four business days of the request (ten business days for requests subject to § 1-214(b),(c)), Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-206(a); no response within the applicable period is deemed a denial.

fees.copy_rule: State agencies: not over $0.25 per page; other agencies: not over $0.50 per page; inspection free; certified copies $1 first page, $0.50 each additional, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212.
fees.waiver_rule: Agency must waive the fee if requester is indigent, or records are found exempt, or in other statutory cases (§ 1-212(d)).

residency.rule_text: FOIA applies to 'every person' without regard to citizenship, § 1-210(a); special limits for incarcerated requesters, § 1-210(c).

appeal.rule_text: Any person denied access may appeal to the FOIC by notice of appeal, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-206(b); FOIC must decide within one year; further appeal to Superior Court under UAPA within 45 days of the FOIC decision notice (§ 4-183(b)). AG plays no role.
